speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance with regard to the new shared parental leave scheme (NSPL) announced on 18 August 2024 (a) what is the rationale for commencing the NSPL on 1 April 2025; (b) whether the Government will consider bringing forward the NSPL commencement date to 2024; and (c) if the commencement date cannot be brought forward, whether there are alternative support measures available to prospective parents who will otherwise miss out on the NSPL benefits.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance what are the planned efforts with the tripartite partners to drive support for the new shared parental leave scheme, especially on the utilisation of paternity leave.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We had considered implementing the new scheme earlier so that more parents can benefit.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, employers had requested for a longer lead time to prepare for this change, as companies need to update their administrative processes and to put in place new measures to manage their employees’ extended absences.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is especially so because the new SPL scheme involves a leave-sharing feature, which requires coordination between both parents and their respective employers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Time is also needed for the Government to effect various legislative and operational changes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We fully understand that parents who miss out on the enhancements could feel disappointed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, the deferred start date is necessary to ensure that all stakeholders involved are ready to implement the changes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Implementing the new SPL from 1 April 2025 strikes a balance between giving employers sufficient time to make the necessary adjustments in this tight labour market and allowing parents to benefit from the enhancements as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: During this transition period, before the new SPL takes effect, we encourage employers to update their manpower and business approaches to facilitate more progressive workplace practices and to foster a more family-friendly culture.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Employers who can provide more than the current legislated provisions, whether in the form of leave or other support, are encouraged to do so as this can position them as employers of choice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government will continue to work closely with the tripartite partners to support the implementation of the enhanced parental leave provisions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will organise webinars for employers to understand the operational details of the scheme and to provide more information on existing grants and resources employers can tap on to strengthen their manpower planning capabilities and to support their operational and system adjustments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our research has shown that utilisation of parental leave is often dependent on workplace support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will work with the tripartite partners to shape workplace norms and culture, including to establish the norm of fathers taking leave to care for and bond with their infants.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will also emphasise the need for good communication and responsible behaviour on the part of both employers and employees.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Employees should be mindful of their employers’ operational needs and act responsibly by informing their employers as early as possible once they know that they are expecting a child.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Employers, on their part, should be facilitative and supportive of employees’ parental leave plans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Employers and employees should work together to put in place covering arrangements that best meet the needs and constraints on both sides.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We need to work together as a society to create a culture that embraces families and children, and supports fathers in playing a greater role in child-raising while meeting employers’ needs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Together, let us build a Singapore Made For Families.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe there are a lot of employers out there who welcome these ideas and are thinking of ways on how to adopt them.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But on the other hand, there will also be employers who adopt a wait-and-see situation to see how the situation develops by the time the implementation is in place next year.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I am thinking, whether the Government is working closely with the tripartite partners to identify the good practices of current and existing employers or those who are already ready to adopt these practices to share and amplify such good practices, so as to encourage more employers to come onboard and embrace this in time and ahead of the timelines?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The answer is, yes, we are working with the employers and the unions on this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they should use the time between now and 1 April 2025 to get their processes in place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, that start date of 1 April 2025 was at the request of the Singapore National Employers' Federation and the other employers that we spoke to – because they needed the time to put this in place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are also, as I mentioned earlier, conducting webinars for the employers because many of the employers do have questions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the engagements that I have had with them, I found that many of the questions are actually operational ones.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are the detailed, technical ones and sometimes, they ask what happens in this situation, what happens in that situation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We thought that the best way to deal with that is to have these webinars for them, so it allows all the employers to come, ask their questions and share their best practices with each other.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Across the Labour Movement, both the younger workers appreciate the move and the older workers similarly understand the reason why this has to be done.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For a workforce that is ageing and could shrink over time, the worry among the older workers or those who already have children and do not intend to have more, their worry is, "I have to cover more duties and I might need to do this for many more years to come if the Government policies work as well as they are supposed to".

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, would the Ministry provide guidance on how employers can better support these workers, the existing ones, in carrying the additional load?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How can some of the support from the Government be better shared with the workers and can we expect further support for these workers?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because in the post-announcement engagements that we have done, a number of employers have asked us how will they cope.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Choo is representing the viewpoint of the older employees; or maybe not older, because it could also be the single employees who will have to take up some of the slack.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That means that frees up the money that they would otherwise have had to pay.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With this money, you could hire other workers to come in as substitutes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And you remunerate and you compensate them for that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, yes, for the period of time when their colleague is away, they have to work harder but at least you are compensating them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also encourage employers to continue to invest in technology and systems that would help with automation, digitalisation – anything that lightens the workload.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because it is not just the Shared Parental Leave; do not forget, there is also the flexible work arrangements – all of which have a common feature, which is this flexibility and how do you replace people or cover in their absence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, these are resources and tools which the employers can tap on.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am trying to get as many Parliamentary Questions (PQs) to be answered today as possible.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I will only allow Members who filed PQs to ask supplementary questions for today.
